policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV main text 'that I should not go down to the pit' renders the qere מִיָּרְדִי (infinitive, 'from my going down'); the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, from among them that go down to the pit' explicitly names the ketiv מיורדי (participle, 'from those going down') as the reading the ASV did not adopt.
